entries.name: x402node Airport Status Check
entries.description: Check a single US airport's live FAA operational status by code (e.g. JFK): any active closures, ground stops, ground delays and arrival delays with reasons and timing, or 'normal' when clear.

inputSchema.airport: string — US airport code, e.g. JFK, LAX, ORD (query param, optional per schema but supply it to check a specific airport)

outputSchema.status: string — 'normal' when clear, otherwise reflects active disruptions
outputSchema.closures: array — active airport closures (empty when none)
outputSchema.groundStops: array — active ground stops (empty when none)
outputSchema.groundDelays: array — active ground delay programs (empty when none)
outputSchema.arrivalDelays: array — active arrival delays with reasons/timing (empty when none)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-check?airport=<US airport code> (x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.005/call, no API key, no body). The airport code goes in the query param; result returns inline in the 200 JSON.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object: {source, country, airport, updateTime, status ('normal' if clear), closures[], groundStops[], groundDelays[], arrivalDelays[], other[]}. When an airport has active FAA disruptions, the relevant arrays hold entries with reason + timing detail; verified paid call for JFK returned status 'normal' with all arrays empty.
quirks: US airports only — this is FAA / NAS operational status, not international (for non-US live boards use /aviation/airport-arrivals or /aviation/airport-departures on the same host).
Input is the ?airport= query param (not a JSON body); accepts common IATA codes like JFK/LAX/ORD.
'status':'normal' with empty arrays means the airport is currently clear — that is a valid successful result, not an error.
For a system-wide sweep of every currently-affected US airport, the sibling GET /aviation/airport-status returns all airports at once (also $0.005); this endpoint is the single-airport lookup.
Real price is fixed $0.005 USDC on Base (5000 atomic units), matching openapi.json x-payment-info and the live 402.
openapi.json also advertises a Solana accept for this host, but the captured live 402 offered only the Base (eip155:8453) rail, which is what is indexed here.

entries.name: x402node Flight Delay Check
entries.description: Quick yes/no delay verdict for a single flight by flight number, with departure/arrival delay minutes and scheduled-vs-revised times when the flight is delayed.

flight.description: Flight number e.g. AA100 (IATA or ICAO). Passed as ?flight= query param.

date.description: Optional date YYYY-MM-DD (?date=). Omit for the current/most-recent instance.

delayed.description: Whether the flight is currently delayed

outputSchema.description: When delayed is true the provider additionally reports departure/arrival delay minutes and scheduled-vs-revised times (per openapi summary); for on-time flights only {flight,delayed} is returned.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/flight-delay?flight=<IATA/ICAO flight number>[&date=YYYY-MM-DD]. No request body; the flight number is a query param. x402 USDC on Base, fixed $0.15/call.
usage.outputShape: JSON: body.flight (echoed number), body.delayed (boolean verdict). For a delayed flight the provider also returns departure/arrival delay minutes and scheduled vs revised times (per the openapi description); a verified on-time call (flight=AA100) returned only {flight:'AA100', delayed:false}. Every response also carries a generic _hint marketing string that is not data.
quirks: Verified paid call (flight=AA100) returned a minimal body {flight,delayed:false} — the delay-minute and scheduled/revised-time fields advertised in the openapi summary only appear when delayed is true, so they were not observed in this on-time run.
Flight number goes in the ?flight= query param, NOT a JSON body (this is a GET).
Fixed price $0.15 USDC on Base (150000 atomic units) — one of x402node's pricier endpoints; the round $0.15 is the real quoted fixed price, not a synthetic probe ceiling.
Every JSON response includes a boilerplate _hint field ('x402 paid endpoints for AI agents...') that is marketing text, not part of the flight data.
openapi.json also advertises a Solana accept (network solana:5eykt4..., payTo 9urRvUx69...); only the Base USDC accept from the live 402 is indexed here.
usage.guide: Check whether a specific flight is delayed. GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/flight-delay?flight=<flight number e.g. AA100> (optionally &date=YYYY-MM-DD); the wallet pays $0.15 USDC on Base automatically via the x402 402 flow. Read body.delayed for the yes/no verdict and body.flight for the echoed number; when body.delayed is true the response also carries departure/arrival delay minutes and scheduled-vs-revised times. Verified on-time (delayed:false) with flight=AA100. Ignore the boilerplate _hint field. For richer status use the sibling /aviation/flight-status or /aviation/flight endpoints.

entries.name: x402node Flight Status
entries.description: Universal flight status lookup by flight number (and optional date): scheduled vs actual departure/arrival times, delay minutes, gate, terminal, runway, baggage carousel, aircraft type, and route distance.

inputSchema.flight: string (required in practice) — flight number, IATA/ICAO, e.g. AA100
inputSchema.date: string (optional) — YYYY-MM-DD to pin a specific date's instance

outputSchema.flights: array of { flight, callSign, status, airline, aircraft, departure{airport,airportName,city,country,terminal,gate,runway,scheduled,revised,scheduledUtc,delayMinutes}, arrival{airport,airportName,city,country,terminal,gate,baggageBelt,runway,scheduled,revised,scheduledUtc,delayMinutes}, distanceKm, lastUpdatedUtc, dataQuality[], source }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/flight-status?flight=<IATA/ICAO number>&date=<YYYY-MM-DD optional> (x402 USDC on Base, fixed $0.15, no API key, no body). Input is the flight= query param; date= is optional.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON: { flight (echoed), count, flights[] }. Each flights[] item: flight, callSign, status (e.g. EnRoute/Expected), airline, aircraft, departure{airport,airportName,city,country,terminal,gate,runway,scheduled,revised,scheduledUtc,delayMinutes}, arrival{...,baggageBelt,...}, distanceKm, lastUpdatedUtc, dataQuality[] (e.g. ['Basic','Live']), source ('x402node-aviation'). Verified live: ?flight=AA100 returned count=2 for AA 100 JFK->LHR (Boeing 787-9) with delayMinutes and scheduled/revised times.
quirks: flight= is documented as optional in OpenAPI but is the required identifier in practice — provide a real flight number (IATA/ICAO, e.g. AA100).
Input goes in query params (GET), not a JSON body.
date= is optional; omitting it returns the nearest current/upcoming instance(s) — the live call returned count=2 (today's and next day's departures of the same flight number).
Fixed price $0.15 USDC on Base (150000 atomic units), not 'Varies'.
Provider also lists a Solana payment option in OpenAPI, but the live 402 accepts captured here is Base USDC only.
dataQuality[] flags how live the record is ('Live' vs 'Basic'); source is 'x402node-aviation' (distinct from StableTravel's FlightAware/Amadeus data).
needs: A flight number in IATA/ICAO form (e.g. AA100); optionally a YYYY-MM-DD date.
usage.guide: Look up flight status with a paid x402 GET. Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/flight-status?flight=<flight number> (e.g. flight=AA100), optionally adding &date=YYYY-MM-DD; the wallet auto-pays the fixed $0.15 USDC quote on Base (no API key, no body). Read the answer from body.flights[] — each item has status, airline, aircraft, departure and arrival objects (scheduled/revised times, delayMinutes, terminal, gate, runway, baggageBelt), distanceKm and dataQuality[]. body.count tells you how many instances matched. Synchronous — no polling.

entries.name: x402node Airport Arrivals Board
entries.description: Live airport arrivals board by IATA code: incoming flights with origin airport, airline, flight number, status, terminal, gate, and scheduled vs revised arrival times.

inputSchema.airport: string (required) — airport IATA code, e.g. JFK, LHR, PEK. Passed as ?airport= query param.

outputSchema.count: number — number of flights in the board
outputSchema.flights: array of { flight (flight number), status (e.g. Arrived/Expected/Unknown), airline, otherAirport (origin IATA), otherCity, terminal, gate, scheduled (local time w/ offset), revised (local time w/ offset or null) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-arrivals?airport=<IATA code> (x402 USDC on Base or Solana, fixed $0.20/call, no API key, no body). The airport IATA code goes in the ?airport= query param; the full arrivals board returns inline in the 200 JSON.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON: { airport (echoed IATA), direction ('arrivals'), count, flights[] , source }. Each flights[] item: flight (flight number, e.g. 'AM 404'), status ('Arrived'|'Expected'|'Unknown'|...), airline, otherAirport (origin IATA), otherCity (often null), terminal, gate (often null), scheduled (local time with UTC offset), revised (local time or null).
usage.quirks: Times are local to the airport with a UTC offset suffix (e.g. '2026-07-29 23:55-04:00'). gate and otherCity are frequently null. Board is a fixed-size snapshot (~30 recent/upcoming arrivals), not a full-day list. Accepts payment on Base OR Solana — either network works.
usage.needs: An airport IATA code (e.g. JFK, LHR, PEK).
usage.guide: Pass a single airport IATA code as ?airport=. Returns the live arrivals board for that airport. No date parameter; it reflects the current board. For per-flight detail use x402node Flight Status; for FAA operational status use x402node Airport Status Check.

entries.name: x402node Airport Departures
entries.description: Live airport departures board by IATA code: upcoming and recently departed flights with destination airport, airline, terminal, gate, scheduled and revised times, and status, from x402node's own aviation aggregation.

inputSchema.airport: Airport IATA code, e.g. JFK, LHR, PEK (query param, effectively required)

outputSchema.flights: array; each: flight (e.g. 'DL 284'), status ('Departed' | 'Expected' | ...), airline, otherAirport (destination IATA), otherCity, terminal, gate, scheduled, revised

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-departures?airport=<IATA code> over x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, fixed $0.20/call, no API key, no request body). Input is a single query param.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object: { airport (echoed IATA), direction ('departures'), count (int), flights[], source ('x402node-aviation') }. Each flights[] item = { flight (formatted, e.g. 'DL 284'), status ('Departed' | 'Expected' | ...), airline (e.g. 'Delta Air Lines'), otherAirport (destination IATA, e.g. 'CDG'), otherCity (often null), terminal (e.g. '4', often null), gate (frequently null), scheduled (ISO-ish local time with offset, e.g. '2026-07-29 23:30-04:00'), revised (same format) }. Observed count=30 for JFK.
quirks: Verified paid 200 with ?airport=JFK: returned 30 flights with airline, destination IATA, terminal, scheduled/revised times and status (Departed/Expected).

Input goes in the airport= query param (GET, no JSON body). A bare GET with no airport= returns only an {_hint} object (no data), so airport= is effectively required despite the OpenAPI marking it optional.
Fixed price: $0.20 USDC = 200000 atomic units (not 'Varies'/dynamic). Live 402 captured BOTH a Base (eip155:8453) and a Solana accept for this amount; paid via Base.
gate is frequently null and otherCity is often null; terminal and revised are usually populated.
Airport code is IATA (JFK/LHR/PEK), not ICAO — differs from the StableTravel FlightAware entries which take ICAO or IATA in a path segment.
Data source is the provider's own 'x402node-aviation' aggregation (a departures board) — distinct from the StableTravel FlightAware/Amadeus entries in this subcategory (not a merge).
Sibling endpoint /aviation/airport-arrivals is the same $0.20 shape for inbound flights.
usage.guide: Get a live departures board for an airport. Issue GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-departures with a query param airport set to the airport's IATA code (e.g. airport=JFK, LHR, PEK). The wallet pays the fixed x402 quote (~$0.20 USDC on Base or Solana) automatically via the 402 flow — no API key and no request body. Read the answer from body.flights[]: each item has flight (formatted flight number), status (Departed/Expected/...), airline, otherAirport (destination IATA), terminal, gate, scheduled and revised times. body.count tells you how many flights are on the board (30 observed for JFK). Synchronous response, no polling.

entries.name: x402node Airport Status (All US Airports)
entries.description: System-wide FAA NAS status sweep: every US airport currently with a closure, ground stop, ground delay or arrival delay, with the reason and timing for each, in a single call.

inputSchema.description: No input required. The bazaar x402 schema advertises an empty queryParams object; this endpoint takes no query params, path params or body.

outputSchema.affectedAirports: number — count of airports currently affected
outputSchema.closures: array of { airport, reason (raw FAA NOTAM/advisory text), start, reopen } — active airport closures (empty when none)
outputSchema.groundStops: array — active ground stops (empty when none)
outputSchema.groundDelays: array — active ground delay programs (empty when none)
outputSchema.arrivalDelays: array — active arrival delays with reasons/timing (empty when none)
outputSchema._hint: string — provider marketing boilerplate, not data

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-status (no query params, no path params, no body). Pay the x402 quote (~$0.005 USDC, Base or Solana rail); the full system-wide result returns inline in the 200 JSON.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object: { source, country ('US'), affectedAirports (number), updateTime (FAA GMT timestamp), closures[], groundStops[], groundDelays[], arrivalDelays[], other[], _hint }. Each entry in the disruption arrays (e.g. closures[]) is an object like { airport, reason (raw FAA advisory text), start, reopen }. Verified paid call returned affectedAirports:7 with 7 populated closures[] (PVD, SNA, LFT, LAX, HNL, LAS, SAN) and empty groundStops/groundDelays/arrivalDelays/other.
quirks: US airports only — this is FAA / NAS operational status, not international.

Takes NO input — it always returns the full system-wide list of currently-affected US airports. For a single named airport use the sibling GET /aviation/airport-check?airport=<code> ('x402node Airport Status Check'), also ~$0.005.
closures[] entries carry the raw FAA advisory/NOTAM text in 'reason' (e.g. '!PVD 07/028 PVD AD AP CLSD...') plus human-readable start/reopen strings; parse rather than display verbatim.
Empty disruption arrays (groundStops[], groundDelays[], arrivalDelays[], other[]) are valid successful results meaning nothing of that type is currently active — not an error.
Real price is fixed $0.005 USDC (5000 atomic units), matching openapi.json x-payment-info and the live 402.
The live 402 offers BOTH a Base (eip155:8453) and a Solana (solana:5eykt4...) accept at the same 5000-unit price; both are indexed. The endpoint description explicitly states 'either network works'.
Every response includes a boilerplate _hint marketing field that is not part of the data.
usage.guide: Get a one-shot, system-wide view of US airport disruptions from official FAA NAS data. Issue GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/airport-status with no parameters or body; the wallet auto-pays the ~$0.005 x402 quote (USDC on Base or Solana). Read affectedAirports for the count, then iterate the closures[], groundStops[], groundDelays[], arrivalDelays[] and other[] arrays — each item names the airport plus the reason (raw FAA advisory text) and timing (start/reopen). Empty arrays mean nothing of that type is active. Synchronous, no polling. US airports only; for a single airport use /aviation/airport-check?airport=<code>.

entries.name: x402node Ground Delays
entries.description: Nationwide FAA feed of every US airport currently under an active ground stop or ground delay program, with the reason and average delay for each.

inputSchema.format: string (optional) — response format hint (?format=); no other input. This is a nationwide feed, so no airport/flight identifier is required.

outputSchema.groundStops: array — airports with active ground stops (each with airport, reason, timing when present); empty when none
outputSchema.groundDelays: array — airports with active ground delay programs (each with airport, reason, average delay when present); empty when none
outputSchema.count: number — total affected airports across ground stops + ground delays (0 when the system is clear)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/ground-delays (x402 USDC on Base, fixed $0.006/call, no API key, no body, no required query params). Optional ?format= hint. Result returns inline in the 200 JSON.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object: {source, country, updateTime, groundStops[], groundDelays[], count}. groundStops[] and groundDelays[] list the currently-affected US airports with their reason and (for delays) average delay; count is the total affected airports. Verified paid call returned {source:'x402node-aviation', country:'US', updateTime:'Thu Jul 30 04:14:28 2026 GMT', groundStops:[], groundDelays:[], count:0} — i.e. no active FAA ground stops/delays at call time, a valid clear result. Response also carries a boilerplate _hint marketing string that is not data.
quirks: System-wide FAA feed — takes NO required input (no airport/flight code); for a single US airport use the sibling /aviation/airport-check, for all currently-disrupted airports (any disruption type) use /aviation/airport-status.
US airports only (FAA / NAS operational data), and scoped specifically to ground stops + ground delay programs.
count:0 with empty groundStops[]/groundDelays[] means no airports are currently affected — a valid successful result, not an error.
Fixed price $0.006 USDC on Base (6000 atomic units), matching openapi.json x-payment-info and the live 402; not 'Varies'.
Every JSON response includes a boilerplate _hint field ('x402 paid endpoints for AI agents...') that is marketing text, not part of the data.

The live 402 and openapi also advertise a Solana accept (network solana:5eykt4..., asset EPjFWdd5..., payTo 9urRvUx69..., amount 6000); only the Base USDC accept is indexed here, matching the sibling x402node aviation entries.
usage.guide: Get a nationwide snapshot of US FAA ground stops and ground delay programs. Issue GET https://api.x402node.dev/aviation/ground-delays and let the wallet pay the x402 quote (~$0.006 USDC on Base, no API key, no body, no required params). Read the 200 JSON: groundStops[] lists airports with active ground stops and groundDelays[] lists airports under ground delay programs (each with reason and, for delays, average delay); count is the total affected airports and is 0 when the system is clear; updateTime is the FAA data timestamp. Synchronous — no polling. US airports only. Ignore the boilerplate _hint field. For a single airport use /aviation/airport-check; for all disrupted airports across every disruption type use /aviation/airport-status.

entries.name: Greeneris METAR Aviation Weather
entries.description: Latest decoded METAR surface observation for any ICAO airport worldwide (NOAA AviationWeather.gov) — wind direction/speed/gust (kt), temperature/dewpoint (C), visibility, QNH altimeter (hPa), flight category (VFR/MVFR/IFR/LIFR), plus the raw METAR string; up to 10 airports per call.

accepts.description: Latest decoded METAR observation for any ICAO airport worldwide (NOAA AviationWeather.gov)

ids.description: 1-10 comma-separated ICAO station codes, e.g. KJFK,LFPG,EGLL

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/aviation/metar?ids=<ICAO codes>. Required query param ids = 1-10 comma-separated ICAO airport codes (e.g. KJFK,LFPG,EGLL). Pay via x402 (exact, Base USDC, $0.002 flat per call regardless of how many airports). No API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { count: integer, metars[]{ icao, name, observed_utc, temp_c, dewpoint_c, wind_dir_deg, wind_speed_kt, wind_gust_kt(nullable), visibility, altimeter_hpa, flight_category (VFR|MVFR|IFR|LIFR), raw, lat, lon }, source } }
quirks: Result is wrapped in { ok, data:{...} } — the actual payload is under `data` (the 402 bazaar example shows the inner object un-wrapped, but the live 200 wraps it).
ids is REQUIRED: 1-10 comma-separated ICAO codes (4-letter airport identifiers, e.g. KJFK, LFPG, EGLL). count echoes how many observations were returned.
Flat $0.002 per call whether you request 1 or 10 airports — batch up to 10 ICAO codes in one call for the best value.
flight_category is the aviation VFR/MVFR/IFR/LIFR classification derived from ceiling + visibility. wind_gust_kt is null when no gust is reported.
Observations refresh every 30-60 min at the source; server caches ~5 min. observed_utc is the actual observation time, which can lag the current time.
Query schema advertises methods GET|HEAD|DELETE; GET is the read. Data sourced from NOAA AviationWeather.gov (US Government, public domain).
Price $0.002 = atomic amount 2000 USDC (6 decimals) on Base.
usage.guide: Get the latest decoded METAR surface observation for any ICAO airport worldwide. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/aviation/metar?ids=<codes> where ids is 1-10 comma-separated ICAO airport codes (e.g. KJFK,LFPG,EGLL). Pay via x402 exact (Base USDC, $0.002 flat, up to 10 airports per call), no API key. Data from NOAA AviationWeather.gov (public domain).

entries.name: 2s Nearby Airports
entries.description: Find airports within a radius of a latitude/longitude coordinate, sorted by great-circle distance. Pay-per-call x402.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US).

scheduled_service.description: Optional; when true, only commercial-service airports.

outputSchema.description: Wrapped response: results live under data.items[]; billing/settlement under meta.

distanceKm.description: Great-circle distance to (lat, lon) in km; results sorted ascending.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/airport/near?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&radius_km={radius_km}&limit={limit} (x402 paid, no request body). radius_km/limit optional; optional filters: type, country, scheduled_service.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] is the airport list sorted by distanceKm ascending; each item has id, ident, name, type (large_airport|medium_airport|small_airport|heliport|seaplane_base|balloonport|closed), iataCode, icaoCode, latitude, longitude, elevationFt, isoCountry, isoRegion, municipality, scheduledService, wikipediaLink, distanceKm. body.data.total may be null. body.data.source names the dataset (OurAirports, CC0). body.meta.cost.usd + body.meta.settlement.txHash confirm payment.
quirks: Response is double-wrapped: read airports from body.data.items[] (NOT body.airports, despite the 402 resource.description wording).

Data is OurAirports (CC0), so results include heliports/seaplane bases/closed fields, not just commercial airports — use the type or scheduled_service filter to narrow (e.g. scheduled_service=true for commercial-service airports only).
total is often null (upstream count unknown); rely on items.length.
Same operation as StableTravel FlightAware 'Airports Nearby' but a different provider/dataset (OurAirports vs FlightAware AeroAPI) — kept separate, not merged.
usage.guide: Find airports near a coordinate. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/airport/near with query params lat (-90..90) and lon (-180..180) required; radius_km (1-2000, default 200) and limit (1-100, default 20) optional; optional filters type (large_airport|medium_airport|small_airport|heliport|seaplane_base|balloonport|closed), country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), and scheduled_service (true = commercial-service airports only). No request body. The x402 payment ($0.001 USDC on Base or Solana) is handled by the pay layer. On success (200) read body.data.items[] — an array of airports sorted by distanceKm ascending; each has name, ident, iataCode, icaoCode, type, latitude, longitude, municipality, isoCountry, and distanceKm. Data is sourced from OurAirports (CC0). Verified 2026-07-31 with {lat:40.7128, lon:-74.006, radius_km:200, limit:20} -> HTTP 200, $0.001 charged (tx 0xe1d3da2ad84788894fdc0ff9f6bda864c245d99e89a4f74e35760de6b1a3861b).

type enum: departures | arrivals | scheduled_departures | scheduled_arrivals (default departures)

entries.name: Agentstools Travel Entry Requirements
entries.description: Fused international entry requirements for a passport-country and destination pair — visa requirement + allowed days, passport-validity rule, US State Dept travel advisory level, and current CDC travel-health notices combined into one cited JSON, billed per call over x402.

passport_country.description: Passport country name, ISO2 or ISO3 code (e.g. US, USA, United States).

destination.description: Destination country name, ISO2 or ISO3 code (e.g. TH, THA, Thailand).

outputSchema.description: passport_country{iso2,iso3,name}, destination{iso2,iso3,name}, purpose (nullable), visa{requirement,requirement_label,allowed_days,visa_required,description,source}, passport_validity_rule{rule,indicative}, advisory (nullable {level,level_label,updated,source}), health_notices[]{level,title,url,published,scope,source}, required_docs[] (string), entry_notes[] (string), sources{providers[],errors,partial}, attribution[] (string), disclaimer (string)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/travel/entry?passport_country=<ISO2/ISO3/name>&destination=<ISO2/ISO3/name> (optional &purpose=<text>) — no request body; pay $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base. Result returned synchronously in the 200 JSON body.
usage.outputShape: Sync JSON: passport_country{iso2,iso3,name}, destination{iso2,iso3,name}, purpose (null unless supplied), visa{requirement,requirement_label,allowed_days,visa_required (bool),description,source:'visa_matrix'}, passport_validity_rule{rule,indicative}, advisory (null or {level,level_label,updated,source:'state_advisory'}), health_notices[]{level,title,url,published,scope,source:'cdc_health'}, required_docs[], entry_notes[], sources{providers[],errors{},partial (bool)}, attribution[], disclaimer.
quirks: Both inputs are GET query params (passport_country, destination required; purpose optional) — no request body. Accepts country name, ISO2 or ISO3.
402 body is empty {}; the x402 challenge (accepts) is served in the 'payment-required' response header (base64 JSON).
advisory can be null (was null for US->Thailand at index time despite the 402 example showing a level-1 advisory); health_notices returned 3 global CDC notices.

Data is a FUSION of multiple sources: visa from the community Passport Index dataset (visa_matrix, INDICATIVE only), advisory from US State Dept (state_advisory), health from US CDC (cdc_health). sources.partial flags when a provider failed.
Explicitly informational, NOT immigration/visa/legal advice — response carries a disclaimer and attribution; visa data is community-sourced and indicative.
x402 paid $0.03 USDC on Base only (network eip155:8453, asset 0x833589..., payTo 0xF22e558a...); no Solana option, no API key / no sign-in.
Sibling endpoints /travel/visa, /travel/health, /travel/advisory are separate single-source ops, indexed separately.
usage.guide: To get fused international entry requirements for a trip: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/travel/entry with query params passport_country (the traveler's passport country, as a name or ISO2/ISO3 code) and destination (the destination country, name or ISO code); optionally purpose (e.g. tourism). Pay $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base (no API key). Read the 200 JSON: visa{} gives the visa requirement, allowed_days and whether a visa is required; passport_validity_rule gives the passport-validity requirement; advisory (may be null) gives the US State Dept travel advisory level; health_notices[] lists current CDC travel-health notices; required_docs[] and entry_notes[] summarize what to bring/verify. Treat visa data as INDICATIVE (community dataset) — the response includes a disclaimer and source attribution.
